display.title: Episode 393: The King Is Watching (Elul)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's first show of Elul: chase away bad thoughts with holy ones, Shema with a visiting family, and the story of a rabbi who taught a hungry coachman that the King is always watching.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the first week of Elul 5749. Uncle Yossi explains that in Elul Hashem is like a King in the field, close and smiling at us, so we should be extra careful, beginning with our thoughts. The yetzer hara is tricky: a bad thought leads to bad words and then bad deeds. But he is also a coward, and we chase him away by thinking of something holy instead: the Shema, picturing Hashem's four-letter name (Shivisi Hashem), and the Twelve Pesukim, our secret weapon. After the Hakochainik march, a father brings all his children to Studio 604 to lead the Shema. Story time tells of old Rabbi Yitzchak traveling through a forest with a hungry coachman. When the coachman climbs the fence of the king's apple orchard and asks the rabbi to keep watch, the rabbi calls out 'He's watching!' and later explains that he meant the King of all kings. The show ends with an offer from Tzivos Hashem to help children enroll in a yeshiva for the new school year.
display.lesson: Hashem, the King of all kings, sees everything we do and even hears our thoughts, so fill your mind with good thoughts and never take what is not yours.

segments.title: Elul: Chasing Away the Yetzer Hara with Good Thoughts
segments.summary: With the King so close in Elul, we guard our thoughts, chase away the yetzer hara, and replace bad thoughts with the Shema, Hashem's name and the Twelve Pesukim.

segments.title: The King Is Watching
segments.summary: A hungry coachman tries to steal apples from the king's orchard; Rabbi Yitzchak's warning 'He's watching!' teaches him that Hashem sees everything.

segments.title: Tzivos Hashem helps children enroll in a yeshiva
